subject: Recap + next steps: region pinning, data residency & failover
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Moore <daniel.moore@acmebank.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: region pinning, data residency & failover

Hi Daniel and Priya -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we covered and the actions we proposed so we can align on next steps:

Summary from call:
- Primary ask: ensure inference data and model-related artifacts for Acme Bank are pinned to the US region for all US customers.
- Cross-region failover: Acme wants a clear failover strategy for disasters (automatic vs manual), but must preserve data residency guarantees.
- Backups & snapshots: confirmation on whether backups must remain in-region or can be replicated cross-region under contractual controls.
- PII/data classification: need to confirm what data you consider PII and any special handling (masking/tokenization, retention limits).
- Logging & audit: specify retention windows for request logs and audit trails and whether logs may be aggregated or must be kept per-region.

Questions for Acme (please confirm):
1) Primary region: Do you want Redwood to route all production inference and persisted artifacts for Acme to a specific US region (e.g., us-east-1)?
2) Failover RTO/RPO: What are your RTO/RPO targets for the inference service in a regional outage?
3) Backups/replication: Must backups remain in-region at all times, or is cross-region replication allowed if copies are encrypted and access-controlled?
4) Retention: What retention period is required for logs, request traces, and model request payloads (internal default is 90 days)?
5) Key management: Will you require customer-managed KMS keys for at-rest encryption (recommended for regulated customers)?

What we can provide now:
- Region pinning: per-customer routing policy that pins traffic to a selected region and enforces model version pinning.
- Backups: by default stored in-region; we support configurable snapshot replication and restore workflows.
- Failover options: automated failover (active-active or asynchronous replication) or manual failover with approval gate; we can document tradeoffs.
- Logging: control-plane audit logs are available, and we can export request logs to your S3 bucket for long-term retention.

Attachments: Redwood_Region_Pin_Guide.pdf (technical notes) and Redwood_Security_Compliance_Packet.pdf (SOC2/KMS overview).

Proposed next steps:
- Please answer the 5 questions above so we can scope the architecture.
- I will loop in Vanessa (infra) and Marissa (security/compliance) after you confirm to provide detailed technical notes and contractual language.
- If helpful, propose a follow-up technical call on Friday (Mar 17) to walk through options and timelines.

Thanks - looking forward to your answers.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: region pinning, data residency & failover

Thanks Aditya - appreciate the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Primary region: yes, we want production inference for US customers to be pinned to the US (preferably us-east-1).
- Backups: preference is that backups remain in-region. Cross-region replication is acceptable only if we have contractual approval and the copied data is encrypted with our customer-managed key.
- Failover: we need the ability to fail over to EU as a contingency (we have EU-resident customers). That said, any automatic cross-region failover must honor data residency rules - i.e., EU customer data must never be copied out of the EU. For US customers, we are open to warm standby in EU but want to understand the mechanics.
- Retention: regulatory requirement is 7 years for certain logs. We need a plan for long-term log retention (7 years) and a method to export logs for e-discovery.

Can Vanessa or Marissa confirm whether Redwood supports the following out of the box:
1) Per-customer KMS keys for snapshot encryption?
2) Export pipeline for logs to our S3 with lifecycle rules?

Let's set the follow-up call - Mar 17 (Fri) at 10am ET works for our infra and compliance teams.

- Daniel
Daniel Moore
Senior Director, Cloud Engineering | Acme Bank
daniel.moore@acmebank.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Moore <daniel.moore@acmebank.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: region pinning, data residency & failover

Thanks Daniel - great questions. Quick answers and proposed approach before the Fri call:

1) KMS & backups: We support customer-managed KMS keys for snapshot encryption. Snapshots can be configured to use your KMS key so any replicated copies remain encrypted under that key. Cross-region replication can be enabled but we will note it in the contract (explicit consent).

2) Backups in-region: Default behavior is in-region storage for snapshots and backups. We can enable asynchronous replication to a warm-standby region (e.g., eu-west-1) for faster recovery, but the replication policy is configurable: you can choose to replicate only metadata (no PII), replicate encrypted snapshots, or keep replication off and perform manual snapshot exports.

3) Failover models (tradeoffs):
- Active-passive (recommended for strict residency): Keep primary in US, warm standby in EU that has periodic encrypted snapshots. Failover is manual or controlled via playbook so we avoid inadvertent cross-region writes.
- Active-active: replicate data across regions to reduce RTO, but requires explicit contractual approval for any PII replication and may trigger additional compliance obligations.

4) Logging & retention: Redwood default request-log retention is 90 days in the control plane. For multi-year retention (e.g., 7 years), we recommend exporting logs to your S3 bucket (we support push/export pipelines) where lifecycle rules can be applied. We also support on-demand exports for e-discovery.

Action items I have captured:
- Vanessa: can you prepare a short note on the recommended failover architecture and options (warm standby replication vs active-active) and list any operational constraints?
- Marissa: can you confirm the contractual language and any SOC2/KMS considerations for cross-region replication?
- Daniel / Priya: confirm Mar 17 10am ET for the technical deep-dive.

Linking the relevant materials here for the call prep: https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme-region-pin-guide and INF-1234.

I'll attach the region guide and security packet to this thread again.

Best,
Aditya

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: region pinning, data residency & failover

Hi Daniel / Priya -

Thanks for the detailed questions. A few technical clarifications ahead of Friday's call:

- Region pinning: Redwood routes traffic at the tenant level using routing policies tied to your account. For Acme we can enforce us-east-1 for all US tenant traffic and maintain separate routing for EU tenant traffic. This ensures compute and ephemeral caches are region-local.

- Backups & snapshots: By default, snapshot storage and automated backups remain in the same region as the compute. We support three backup replication modes:
  1) In-region only (default) - recommended for strict residency.
  2) Async replication of encrypted snapshots to warm-standby region (encrypted under your CMK). Metadata only replication is also supported for reduced exposure.
  3) Full cross-region replication (active-active) - requires legal sign-off and may increase exposure for PII.

- KMS: Customer-managed KMS keys are supported. We can configure snapshots and persisted artifacts to be encrypted with your CMK so Redwood does not hold unencrypted key material.

- Logging & export: Control-plane audit logs are retained in-region; request logs can be exported to your S3 (we support S3 at both regional and cross-region endpoints). For 7-year retention, we recommend exporting to your S3 and applying lifecycle rules. We can also provide an S3 export + Glue catalog for easier e-discovery if needed.

- Failover recommendation: For Acme's requirements I recommend Active-Passive (warm standby) with periodic encrypted snapshot replication to the standby region. Failover should be gated via a documented runbook and remediation checklist to prevent accidental PII replication. For customers who require sub-minute RTO across regions, we can discuss active-active, but that has compliance tradeoffs.

I'll prepare a short diagram and a 1-pager describing the warm-standby failover flow and the knobs for snapshot replication. Sharing that before the Fri call.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
